question: Compare the electrostatic potential due to an electric dipole at a point on its axial line and at a point on its equatorial line, both at the same large distance $r$ from the centre of the dipole. Give reason.

options.A: At the same distance, both axial and equatorial potentials are $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p}{r^2}$
options.B: Axial potential is zero and equatorial potential is $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p}{r^2}$
options.C: Both potentials are zero because the dipole has zero net charge
options.D: On the axial line, $V=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p}{r^2}$ in magnitude; on the equatorial line, $V=0$ because scalar potentials cancel
